newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: BZW Metals calls for expanded LME ring membership.
newsitem.headline: BZW Metals calls for expanded LME ring membership.

text.p: The chairman of BZW Metals and Energy Group called on Monday for the London Metal Exchange (LME) to study the possibility of an expanded membership roll for ring members on the exchange.

Christopher Green said at a copper conference in Singapore the LME must address the sharp reduction in the number of members authorised to deal in the ring, which he said is less than half the 32 present when he joined the market in 1959.
The ring members are responsible for processing orders from all over the world and help determine the official prices of the day for each metal.

"This very structure may be under threat. I believe a case is developing for requiring all clearing members of the LME to contribute to the costs of maintaining this unique establishment ...by themselves becoming ring members and thus eliminating the distinction between these two categories," he said.

Such a change would boost the financial strength of the LME and "eliminate the exploitation of one sector by the other" and focus competition on the idea of providing a better and more reliable service to users of the exchange, Green concluded.
"Trade clearing members who do not conduct business with third parties would be allowed to maintain their status."
BZW Metals and Energy Group is a part of BZW, the investment banking division of Britain's Barclays Bank Plc.
Green said the LME should also seek to widen the delivery system for metals especially in rapidly growing Asian markets.
"The fast growing Southeast Asian and Far Eastern markets have only Singapore for metals other than aluminium," he said.

"So the LME will undoubtedly be hoping for a consensus to develop within Japan towards agreeing eventually other metals for delivery to LME warehouses there," Green said. "A further expanded warehouse system should provide an extra degree of confidence and comfort to users."
The location for additional warehouses in Southeast Asia are under consideration by the LME although work will have to be done in amending or waiving local rules or regulations.
Green added: "The locations themselves must, above all, be wholly acceptable to insurers and bankers as well as members and their customers."
The expansion of the delivery network will help eliminate natural or artificial squeezes and encourage the confidence of consumers and fabricators, he added.
